title: Are All Groups Surjunctive?
exact_target: Does every injective cellular automaton on every group, with any finite alphabet, also reach every configuration?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Shared notation.}$\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$, and $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q,\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ denote the integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers. Any other conventions are specified locally.


Let \(G\) be a group and let \(A\) be a nonempty finite set, called
an alphabet.  A configuration is a function \(x:G\to A\); the set of all
configurations is \(A^G\).  A cellular automaton is a map
\(\tau:A^G\to A^G\) for which there are a finite set \(M\subseteq G\)
and a local rule \(\mu:A^M\to A\) satisfying
\[
 \tau(x)(g)=\mu\bigl((x(gm))_{m\in M}\bigr)
       \quad (x\in A^G,\ g\in G).
\]
Thus the same finite local rule applies at every group element.
The group \(G\) is surjunctive if every such injective map is surjective,
for every nonempty finite alphabet.
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Is every group \(G\) surjunctive?  Explicitly, for every group
\(G\), every nonempty finite alphabet \(A\), every finite memory set
\(M\subseteq G\), and every local rule \(\mu:A^M\to A\), is the
associated map \(\tau:A^G\to A^G\) surjective whenever it is injective? \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06586}{[S2]}

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does every injective cellular automaton on every group, with any finite alphabet, also reach every configuration?

\item[S2] Lewis Bowen and Michael Chapman, \emph{Surjunctivity does not characterize cosoficity of invariant random subgroups}, arXiv:2511.06586 (2025), abstract and Section 1. \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06586}.
\end{description}
